title: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination found
source_used: The Times of India, relaying the Wall Street Journal (1 Oct 2026) and an OpenAI statement
key_facts: OpenAI dismissed three safety-team researchers, named by the WSJ as Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, after an internal investigation found they violated policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information.
An OpenAI spokesperson said the three "mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures".

The WSJ reported they were accused of sharing confidential information with outside AI safety organisations, including non-profit evaluators; Korbak had said he was OpenAI's technical contact for METR and Redwood Research during their investigation of the Hugging Face agent incident.
Wang and Balesni worked on alignment; none of the three had commented, per the WSJ.
OpenAI had let METR staff and a Redwood Research contractor work inside its offices for six days after the Hugging Face breach; METR later published a report.
OpenAI this week shelved the launch of GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns and says it has added agent-misbehaviour monitoring and stronger testing guardrails.
quote_evidence: "We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," an OpenAI spokesperson said.
According to a Wall Street Journal report, the three researchers are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, all of whom worked on safety and alignment-related efforts at the company.
why_it_matters_hint: OpenAI has punished the staff who liaised with outside safety auditors, days after inviting those auditors in.
notes: Times of India recap of 4 Oct adds no new facts beyond the WSJ exclusive of 1 Oct and OpenAI's statement already carried then (Forbes, CBS, TechCrunch 1 Oct). Stale by the window rule. WSJ link not given by TOI.
